searchText: (Context: EIP-5081 and text (<#823588372743323658>) with Micah post-ACD) The "two account writes" concerns both nonce increase and balance change, for two separate accounts right? [Screenshot source: https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/some-medium-term-dust-cleanup-ideas/6287] Given the balance and nonce are tightly coupled here, *could* a lookup (and write) be cheaper than two independent reads? "after calling account, treat nonce as if it's semi-warm", or are the issues: [1] balances and nonces are stored elsewhere so looking up one doesn't help you look up the other [2] discounts-for-warmth are intended to correspond with data being in (hardware) memory, hence should occur only after a read has already occurred <@339771292884664320> thanks for providing input. Can you also help me better understand how this affects/will be affected by the expirable transaction. I vaguely understand there is a correlation between nonce+balance affects transaction validability but I do not fully understand your explanation. Oh, just saw your response, <@339771292884664320> https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-5081-expirable-transaction/9208/13 I'm just asking a more generic question: "how much more work is updating balance+nonce compared to just balance" The EVM isn't aware of transaction typing as far as I'm aware too, so I don't think contracts could have an alternate path of execution for expiring transactions. EIP-2929 already treats account access and storage access differently (it seems to me), so could we do the same for recently-accessed EOA nonces?

excerpts.author: 3xmd1559sporebraytondingo
excerpts.content:
Given the balance and nonce are tightly coupled here, *could* a lookup (and write) be cheaper than two independent reads?

"after calling account, treat nonce as if it's semi-warm", or are the issues:

[1] balances and nonces are stored elsewhere so looking up one doesn't help you look up the other

[2] discounts-for-warmth are intended to correspond with data being in (hardware) memory, hence should occur only after a read has already occurred
